findings.reason: The protected source is the conventional linear bucket solution: Counter records each character once, frequency-indexed buckets avoid a comparison sort, and descending traversal emits each recorded occurrence exactly once. The implementation is concise, clear, and expert interview quality, so no inert candidate is justified.

Metadata consistently identifies public LeetCode problem 451 and its runnable Python string contract. The O(n) time and O(n) space manifest claims match the protected function, while the refreshed Reference preserves the nonempty alphanumeric input domain, case sensitivity, grouped-character requirement, and freedom among equal-frequency groups.

The immutable native source is bound to verified submission 2064919013. It has the same Counter construction, n + 1 bucket allocation, frequency-to-character placement, descending frequency scan, repeated-character pieces, and final join as the protected app-local source; only annotations and the LeetCode class wrapper differ.

The 248-, 992-, and 3968-character tiers span 16x and exercise counting, all frequency buckets, and full output construction. The current source passed all 7 opaque correctness executions and all three performance tiers at 0.92x the reference runtime. A correct comparator that calls the linear string count operation for every occurrence passed every output but failed the runtime-scaling verdict, with a 1.25x aggregate runtime ratio.

The Approach exactly derives and describes the protected target: one frequency count, n + 1 buckets, one placement per distinct character, descending bucket traversal, arbitrary tie order, and O(n) counting, scan, and emission costs. Its alternatives accurately distinguish heap, entry sorting, occurrence sorting, and repeated counting tradeoffs.

The hash-bound modular Reference was checked directly against the live public statement. It now preserves the exact three source outputs, all three explanation sequences and alternative valid strings, the grouping and case-sensitivity traps, both constraints, and the original description order. The legacy substitutions of eetr and cccaaa as primary outputs were corrected.
